title: Automation Systems
hook: I spent four hours last week copying invoices into a spreadsheet. A tool could've done it in seconds.
statement: Get yourself out of the repetitive tasks. If it needs no real decision, it shouldn't need you.
explainer: Every manual task you repeat eats time you could spend on sales, strategy, or rest. And as long as it needs you, you're the bottleneck in your own business.
sop: List every task you repeat weekly with no real decisions in it.
Count how many are Automated out of your Total Tasks.
Pick the most frequent manual one and automate it.
Test it for a week and fix whatever breaks.
Each month, automate the next most repetitive task.
equation_example: 6 tasks Automated out of 10 Total Tasks. 6 ÷ 10 = 60%. Higher means more of the business runs without you touching it. Lower means you're still the one doing all the grunt work.
question: Write down one repetitive task you did by hand this week that a tool could handle.
closing_statement: Every task still done by hand is still a leash.
caption:
Principle Nº 144: Automation Systems
